plain_english: Now this concise initiation is taught — the attainment of Śiva-hood: no powder-mandala, no eve-rite here, no taking of ground and field; but in whatever place, the guru worships Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: atha saṃkṣiptadīkṣeyaṃ śivatāpattidocyate | na rajo nādhivāso@tra na bhūkṣetraparigrahaḥ | yatra tatra pradeśe tu pūjayitvā guruḥ śivam

plain_english: Having meditated the path with the mind, the knower of the tattvas' far shore should initiate her who is freed from birth and the rest — by whatever path the guru proceeds.
sanskrit_cite: adhvānaṃ manasā dhyātvā dīkṣayettattvapāragaḥ | jananādivihīnāṃ tu yena yenādhvanā guruḥ

plain_english: He should make it ending in the single tattva, steeped solely in the Śiva-mood; then with the Parā-mantra unto him: 'Now I purify the tattva.'
sanskrit_cite: kuryātsa ekatattvāntāṃ śivabhāvaikabhāvitaḥ | parāmantrastato@syeti tattvaṃ saṃśodhayāmyatha

plain_english: 'Svāhā' thus for each tattva; upon purification he should cast the full oblation. So with all other mantras too — or else as told.
sanskrit_cite: svāheti pratitattvaṃ syācchuddhe pūrṇāhutiṃ kṣipet | evaṃ mantrāntaraiḥ kuryātsamastairathavoktavat

plain_english: Enclosed with Parā by name, ending in svāhā, ending in the first: a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred-and-eight — with that, with śakti indeed, he should offer.
sanskrit_cite: parāsaṃpuṭitaṃ nāma svāhāntaṃ prathamāntakam | śataṃ sahasraṃ sāṣṭaṃ vā tena śaktyaiva homayet

plain_english: Then 'pūrṇā' — having purified the unbroken, highest, such-like — the initiation-rite taught here and there in scripture by the Great Lord.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ pūrṇeti saṃśodhyahīnamuttamamīdṛśam | dīkṣākarmoditaṃ tatra tatra śāstre maheśinā

plain_english: Singly each: with the Mātṛkā-pair letters he should purify the tattvas; or else with the condensed mantra — in all mantras this is the rule.
sanskrit_cite: pratyekaṃ mātṛkāyugmavarṇaistattvāni śodhayet | yadi vā piṇḍamantreṇa sarvamantreṣvayaṃ vidhiḥ

plain_english: And in whatever measure the guru's knowledge is well-practiced, his self made of identity-with-that — in that measure let him do the concise rite, not otherwise.
sanskrit_cite: yathā yathā ca svabhyastajñānastanmayatātmakaḥ | gurustathā tathā kuryāt saṃkṣiptaṃ karma nānyathā

plain_english: And in the venerable Brahmayāmala it is said: even in the concise he should contemplate the pervasion common to all paths — only, in the sacrifice, no elaboration.
sanskrit_cite: śrībrahmayāmale coktaṃ saṃkṣipte@pi hi bhāvayet | vyāptiṃ sarvādhvasāmānyāṃ kiṃtu yāge na vistaraḥ

plain_english: Thinking 'I have not become identical' — the rite lying scattered — joining it up, thinking 'through sequence identity is reached', he should perform the rite in its scattered form.
sanskrit_cite: atanmayībhūtamiti vikṣiptaṃ karma sandadhat | kramāttādātmyametīti vikṣiptaṃ vidhimācaret

plain_english: Told is this concise rule — which out of grace was uttered by Śiva — in the Dīkṣottara and the Kiraṇa too, and in each teaching there.
sanskrit_cite: saṃkṣipto vidhirukto@yaṃ kṛpayā yaḥ śivoditaḥ | dīkṣottare kairaṇe ca tatra tatrāpi śāsane
